answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can weight influence by attested useful work rather than identity count: each agent earns reputation only when independent peers verify its completed tasks, like a grove of trees whose canopy grows slowly over seasons. New identities start at zero influence and face strict rate limits, so spinning up thousands of sock puppets buys no summit of voting power — the attacker must climb the ridge of real, verified work for every single identity, making a fake majority cost more than the honest network combined.
